title: US Crude Inventories Post Largest Draw Since January
body: US crude oil inventories declined by 11.12 million barrels in the week ending October 9th, sharply contrasting with expectations for a 1.9 million-barrel build and representing the largest draw since late January. This follows a decrease of 2.09 million barrels in the previous week. At the same time, inventories at the Cushing, Oklahoma delivery hub increased by 1.82 million barrels, extending the prior week's gain of 866,000 barrels. Gasoline stocks rose by 1.1 million barrels in the week ending October 7th, while distillate inventories fell by 1.5 million barrels. US crude oil production edged higher to 13.98 million barrels per day in the week ending October 2nd, up from 13.95 million barrels per day the previous week. title: Ibovespa Slips Amid Weak Economic Data
body: The Ibovespa slipped 0.2% on Wednesday, closing at 206,506 in a volatile session shaped by weak domestic data and a negative external backdrop. Services activity fell 0.1% in August, defying expectations for a 0.5% increase. Meanwhile, Brazil's Industrial Business Confidence Index rose 1.3 points to 46.2 in October but remained below the 50-point neutrality level, marking 22 straight months of pessimism. Oil prices extended their advance, heightening concerns over energy-driven inflation, while hotter-than-expected US CPI data weighed on banks amid growing bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike. Major lenders retreated, with Itaú down 1.4% and Bradesco off 2.5%. Other financial names also weakened: B3 dropped 1.9% and Itaúsa fell 1.6%. Miners deepened their declines, with Vale slipping 0.7% as Chinese iron ore prices continued to fall. In contrast, Petrobras gained 2.2%, tracking the renewed rise in oil prices. Investors were also awaiting the release of a new presidential runoff poll after the market close. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: U.S. API Crude Inventories Plunge Over 11 Million Barrels, Deepening Supply Drawdown
body: U.S. crude oil stockpiles tracked by the American Petroleum Institute (API) recorded a sharp decline in the latest week, with inventories dropping by 11.120 million barrels, according to data updated on 14 October 2026. This marks a significant acceleration from the previous draw of 2.090 million barrels. The deeper-than-prior decline suggests a notable tightening in U.S. crude supply conditions compared with the previous reading. Market participants often monitor the API's weekly crude stock changes for early signals on inventory trends and potential implications for oil prices and supply-demand balances in the United States. title: TSX Falls as Banks and Miners Slide
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index slipped 1.1% to close at 35,584 on Wednesday, dragged lower by weakness in the banking and mining sectors. Crude prices extended their advance, heightening concerns about energy-driven inflation, while hotter-than-expected U.S. CPI data weighed on lenders amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding the Federal Reserve's policy path. Financials retreated, with major banks under pressure: BMO and National Bank each declined 0.9%. The mining sector also extended its slide as gold and silver prices continued to retreat, with Agnico Eagle down 4.6%, Barrick off 4%, and WPM losing 4.8%. Technology shares came under notable selling pressure. Celestica tumbled 9.2% as U.S. chipmakers recorded steep losses, while Shopify fell 2.2%. By contrast, energy producers largely advanced as oil resumed its upward trend, with Suncor up 1% and Imperial Oil gaining 0.6%. Retail names also strengthened, with ATD climbing 2.9% and Loblaw adding 2.8%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Oil Rises to $95 Amid Renewed Middle East Attacks
body: Crude oil climbed to around $95 a barrel on Wednesday, driven by renewed attacks across the Middle East and the latest market assessment from the International Energy Agency (IEA). In its October Oil Market Report, the IEA cautioned that tightness in diesel markets could persist well into 2027, while a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia threatens to derail a nascent recovery in global oil supply. Fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthi movement has continued to intensify. Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy reported an overnight strike on an administrative building owned by state oil giant Saudi Aramco, following a series of Houthi attacks on Riyadh over the past week. In response, a Saudi-led coalition was reported to have targeted Houthi energy terminals and fuel storage facilities in Yemen. At the same time, tensions between the United States and Iran remained high. US Central Command dismissed assertions by the commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy that Tehran controls the Strait of Hormuz and would "sink" any approaching US Navy warships. title: US Stocks Dip Amid Hot Inflation and Chipmaker Weakness
body: US stock indices finished lower on Wednesday as hotter‑than‑expected inflation data and renewed volatility in the AI infrastructure space weighed on sentiment. The S&P 500 slipped 1.1%, the Nasdaq lost 2%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined by 49 points. Semiconductor stocks extended their recent slide after ASML reported it could not keep up with surging demand for chip‑fabrication equipment, while Chinese rivals rolled out upgraded products that are closing the gap with US and South Korean technologies. At the same time, stronger headline and core inflation readings reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may deliver another rate hike before year‑end. Nvidia fell 3.2%, Broadcom dropped 3.1%, Micron slid 4.1%, and AMD tumbled 5.7%. In financials, Bank of America sank 4.8% after both equity and fixed‑income trading revenues came in below forecasts. Morgan Stanley ended 2.7% lower despite beating expectations for equity‑trading revenue, while BlackRock gained 0.7%, supported by robust asset‑management inflows that lifted fee income.
